Index: .github/workflows/ci.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/ci.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/ci.yml	
@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+name: CI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  pull_request:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+jobs:
+  test:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Check out repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Set up Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+          cache: npm
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Run tests
+        run: npm test

Index: package.json
===================================================================
--- package.json	
+++ package.json	
@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+{
+  "name": "ci-cache-demo",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "description": "Demo project showing GitHub Actions dependency caching",
+  "private": true,
+  "type": "module",
+  "scripts": {
+    "test": "node --test"
+  },
+  "devDependencies": {
+    "is-odd": "3.0.1"
+  }
+}

parts.text:
Done. I chose the Node.js ecosystem.

Files added:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1` — CI on push/PR that runs `npm ci` and `npm test`.
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `test/odd.test.js`, `.gitignore` — minimal project so the workflow is functional.

Caching mechanism: `actions/setup-node@v4` with `cache: npm` caches the global npm cache (`~/.npm`), keyed on `package-lock.json`'s hash. Repeat runs restore the cache so `npm ci` skips re-downloading packages, and the cache is invalidated automatically when the lockfile changes. `npm ci` (not `install`) is used to guarantee the lockfile is respected.
